text_blocks.snippet: Breakthrough COVID-19 infections refer to cases where individuals who are fully vaccinated against COVID-19 still contract the virus. While vaccination provides a high degree of protection against severe illness, hospitalization, and death, it doesn't completely eliminate the risk of infection.

list.title: Definition:
list.snippet: A breakthrough infection is diagnosed when someone who is fully vaccinated (and sometimes boosted) tests positive for COVID-19 more than 14 days after completing their vaccination series according to the American Medical Association.

list.title: Frequency:
list.snippet: Breakthrough infections are not uncommon, but they are generally less severe than infections in unvaccinated individuals. A study from BPKIHS found that 6.2% of COVID-19 cases were breakthrough infections.
